claim: Population firing rate (per functional group, per area) correlates with LFP band power in the same trial, within session, at a rate well above chance after Holm-Bonferroni/BH-FDR correction across the full (condition_group x area x func_group x band) family -- 19/480 cells survive Holm, 142/480 survive BH-FDR. Concentrated in high_gamma (12/19 Holm survivors) and the stim condition group (13/19).
method: within-session Pearson r (population rate vs band power, trial-matched) against a trial-mismatch shuffle null (N=200); per-session hit at |Z|>=1.96; cross-session hit rate tested via exact binomial vs alpha=0.05; Holm-Bonferroni + BH-FDR across the n_sessions>=3 family (480 cells).
notes: Contrasts with all six earlier connectivity methods this week (coherency, Granger LFP-LFP, TE, PPC, Granger SPK-SPK) which came back null (0/N) after pool-before-test designs -- this is the first pool-after-test analysis run to completion on this corpus and it recovers a real, corrected group-level effect.
Session counts behind individual Holm survivors (hit-rate table) are small (4-8 of up to 20) -- read per-cell n_sessions before citing any single row.

GLMM (fit_population_firing_lfp_power_glmm.py, MixedLM REML, session random intercept, subject additive fixed effect, same backbone as fig05): band is the dominant factor (high_gamma/low_gamma >> theta/alpha/beta, Holm p<1e-5); O+ units are LESS coupled than Null or S+ units (Holm p<2e-5, counter to a naive prior); MT/MST differ from FEF/PFC/TEO; condition group (baseline/stim/omission) has no detectable effect.
